title: The 3 Best Robot Lawn Mowers Under $1,500 in 2026
h1: The 3 Best Robot Lawn Mowers Under $1,500 in 2026
metaDescription: Our 3 picks for robot lawn mowers under $1,500 in 2026, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at robot lawn mowers under $1,500 in 2026 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Robomow RS630
products.blurb: Key specs: 3/4-acre recommended, 1.25-acre maximum coverage, 22-inch cutting width with twin blades, Rated for slopes up to 20 degrees.
strengths: Largest coverage ceiling available before crossing into GPS-based premium pricing
22-inch cutting width covers more ground per pass than narrower competitors
Edge mode noticeably reduces manual trimming around the lawn perimeter
Frequently discounted into the upper part of this budget during sales
limitations: List price sits at the top of this tier, so waiting for a sale often matters
No GPS multi-zone routing, still wire-based navigation
20-degree slope rating limits it on genuinely steep terrain
features: Rated for slopes up to 20 degrees

products.name: Worx Landroid M (WR147)
products.blurb: Key specs: 1/4-acre (10,890 sq ft) coverage, AIA narrow-passage navigation, 20V Power Share battery.
strengths: Narrow-passage navigation is useful for yards split into multiple sections
Power Share battery adds cross-tool value for existing Worx owners
Lower price makes it a lower-risk first robot mower purchase
limitations: Smaller coverage ceiling than the RS630, better suited to smaller lots
No wide cutting width or GPS routing for larger, complex lawns
features: Typically well under $1,000 at full list price
